key_insight: SurgRec provides a scalable, reproducible pretraining recipe for surgical video understanding, demonstrating that large multi-source pretraining (10,535 videos, 214.5M frames) and two self-supervised variants (SurgRec-MAE, SurgRec-JEPA) materially improve downstream surgical tasks.
problem_solved: Addresses limited data scale, narrow procedural diversity, and inconsistent/reproducibility-lacking training pipelines in surgical foundation models that impede generalization and fair benchmarking.
method: Curate a large multi-source surgical video corpus (10,535 videos, 214.5M frames) to increase scale and procedural diversity.
Design a reproducible pretraining recipe and pipeline, instantiated with two self-supervised variants: SurgRec-MAE (masked autoencoding) and SurgRec-JEPA (joint-embedding predictive architecture).
Standardize evaluation protocols and benchmarks for consistent comparison and transfer to downstream surgical tasks (e.g., phase recognition, tool detection).
impact: Enables AI/ML practitioners to build more generalizable surgical foundation models using a reproducible, scalable pretraining pipeline and provides standardized benchmarks to accelerate fair comparison and practical deployment in computer-assisted interventions.
visual_elements: Corpus overview chart: stacked bar or pie showing video sources, procedure types, and total frames (10,535 videos, 214.5M frames).
Model comparison diagram: side-by-side schematic of SurgRec-MAE vs SurgRec-JEPA highlighting each pretraining objective.
Training pipeline flowchart: data curation → pretraining → standardized evaluation (emphasize reproducibility checkpoints).
Benchmark performance plot: radar or bar chart comparing downstream task gains (phase recognition, tool detection, etc.) against prior baselines.
paper_title: Scaling Video Pretraining for Surgical Foundation Models
paper_authors: Sicheng Lu, Zikai Xiao, Jianhui Wei, Danyu Sun, Qi Lu
